html:
The global order is significantly impacted today by escalating tensions around the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran stating that it will not reopen the crucial shipping route without the United States meeting all of Tehran's conditions. This follows reports of an Iranian missile attack on an ADNOC tanker in the strait, while the Trump administration indicates it is "only semi-negotiating" with Iran.

Middle East Diplomacy & Security: Netanyahu has officially rejected Trump's 15-point Gaza peace plan, with the Trump administration reportedly viewing this as campaign rhetoric ahead of a general election. The head of Trump's board, however, called Netanyahu's rejection the "only way forward." Amidst these developments, Mohsen Rezaei, a former IRGC commander, has been appointed as Iran's top security official, and Iran describes Israel as the "greatest threat to regional security." A new joint defense agreement, dubbed the "Mecca Pact," has been signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan, with observers suggesting it aims to prevent Iran and Israel from regional dominance.

Russia-Ukraine Conflict: A Ukrainian drone strike deep into Russia killed at least 13 people and injured 75, marking one of the deadliest such attacks since Moscow's full-scale invasion. This comes as reports suggest Putin faces a "humiliating military crisis" and is enacting "desperate plots" to mobilize more fighters, with the Kremlin allegedly pressganging recruits. Separately, Syria has announced a deal with Moscow concerning the future of Russian bases in the country, effectively ending their role as military outposts.

Global Economy & Energy Markets: Oil prices are rising amidst uncertainty over the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, as Iran and Oman continue talks for a safe shipping route. Australia's falling house prices are seen by the RBA's governor, Michele Bullock, as an "easing" property market that makes another interest rate hike less likely. In Europe, warm rivers and low water levels, amidst its fifth heatwave of the summer, are forcing nuclear power plants to reduce output, raising concerns for grids and prices.

Climate & Natural Disasters: Global oceans recorded their hottest July on record, partly fueled by developing El Niño conditions. Much of Europe, including England, is bracing for high temperatures, with droughts expected to be declared in more areas of England. In Colombia, a powerful 7.4 magnitude earthquake has killed at least 20 people and prompted evacuations. Monsoon rains in India's Assam have caused floods, killing 100 people and displacing thousands, while Typhoon Dolphin made landfall in eastern China, forcing the evacuation of hundreds of thousands and canceling over 1,000 flights.

International Security & Justice: Suspected crime boss Daniel Kinahan, one of the world's most wanted men, has spent his first night in custody in Ireland after his extradition from Dubai. In Colombia, an alleged rebel leader, Hernando Forero Mosquera, was killed in a military operation just days after the new president was sworn in. Additionally, the trial of an ex-street gang leader accused of masterminding Tupac Shakur's 1996 murder is set to begin in Las Vegas nearly 30 years after the crime.
